item.title: [hackernews] AI-generated posters don’t have to be horrible
item.description: A Hacker News submission arguing that AI-generated posters don't have to be as bad as they usually are. The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available, so the specific techniques or examples the author uses can't be confirmed.

item.title: [github_trending] google/ax
item.description: AX is Google's open-source declarative orchestrator for agent workloads: you define Workspaces and Tasks in YAML, and it sandboxes them, fences their network, and schedules them across a cluster on top of Agent Substrate, with the project claiming billions of tasks per cluster. Its Kubernetes-like workflow should appeal to teams running autonomous agents in bulk, though the core concepts and protocols are still evolving and breaking changes are expected before a stable release.

item.title: [producthunt] Jev
item.description: Jev is a newly listed Product Hunt tool that positions itself as a way to make fast, structured AI decisions for software automation. Beyond that one-line pitch, the listing gives no implementation details, pricing, or usage information, so developers curious about AI-driven automation will have to open the product page themselves to judge whether it fits their stack.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A developer recounts using Cursor from April 2025 at $20 a month until April 2026, when his company's China region replaced it with OpenAI Codex after Cursor shifted from fixed licensing to usage-based billing with higher, less predictable costs. He credits Cursor's in-editor Tab completion, Cmd+K and Agent and Plan modes, but says Codex feels less like an IDE and more like a super Agent.

It works as a quick scan of the day's tech and business news; each item's details aren't expanded here.

item.title: [infoq] Meta 开源 Astryx：面向 Agent 的 React 设计系统
item.description: Meta has open-sourced Astryx Beta, a React 19 design system it built internally over eight years, shipping 150-plus accessible components, customizable CSS design tokens, and a CLI plus MCP toolchain aimed at both engineers and AI agents. Built on Meta's StyleX compiler, it keeps component behavior and accessibility separate from styling and can export component source via a swizzle command, making it worth a look for frontend teams wiring agents into React apps.

item.title: [v2ex] [问与答] 目前有什么稳定的调用 Claude 的方式吗？
item.description: A V2EX user asks for a reliable way to call Claude, mainly for writing papers: after a year on a first-party account, four were banned last month, and pay-as-you-go API pricing is too expensive since the old subscription covered only about one million output tokens a month. The only option floated is opencode, so the thread is useful to anyone hunting for a stable, cost-sensitive Claude route.

Anyone wanting a consistent set of robot avatars can copy it as-is.

item.description: A Juejin article tackles the interview question "AI can already write 80% of the code, so why does the company still need you?" It contrasts 2026 interviews with those two years ago, when candidates hand-wrote a Promise or explained React Fiber internals; today interviewers assume AI use and probe something else. item.title: [infoq] 不受控的 Agent ，凭什么上生产系统？
item.description: This InfoQ piece asks why uncontrolled agents struggle to reach production, citing a United Airlines chatbot that told a customer the wrong travel-credit expiry and Gartner's forecast that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by end-2027. It introduces Harness Engineering and Graph Engineering, arguing the model only supplies capability while loops, tool dispatch, memory and guardrails decide deployability.

item.title: [v2ex] [ WATCH] 国行 iPhone air 尝试用海外 esim 给港版 apple watch 开通蜂窝失败记录
item.description: A user tried to enable cellular on a Hong Kong Apple Watch Ultra 4 with an overseas eSIM. Since that model needs iOS 27 to pair and AnyGo location spoofing couldn't beat the region lock, he downgraded to iOS 26.6.1 RC because Wloc doesn't support the iOS 27 release. A CSL prepaid card wouldn't allow Watch cellular, but a European carrier's monthly plan added fine — yet after upgrading back to iOS 27, activation still failed, which he attributes to roaming limits or the geo-fence.

item.title: [hackernews] I built non-autoregressive decision models with RL a year ago
item.description: A developer says he built non-autoregressive decision models with RL a year ago: one forward pass covers 100+ languages at roughly 33ms on GPU, built with RLCD and proper scoring rules by Convai Innovations. The point is skipping token-by-token decoding and folding multilingual inference into a single pass, which matters to anyone dealing with latency-sensitive models.

item.description: Alibaba's open-source AI code review tool, Open Code Review (alibaba/open-code-review), gained over 14,000 stars in a single week to top GitHub Trending's weekly chart and pass 40,000 stars, overtaking Arthas and Nacos as the most-starred project in Alibaba's GitHub org. It pairs deterministic engineering — file filtering, rule matching, line-number location — with an LLM agent for semantic review; author Li Zhengfeng will detail the million-task production validation at QCon Shanghai.

item.title: [infoq] Cloudflare 测试通过缓存转码来减少存储需求
item.description: Cloudflare has detailed a prototype called Cache Transcoding that compresses eligible uncompressed text — HTML, JSON, CSS and JavaScript — with Zstandard before it lands on disk, then decompresses it when serving. Compression happens once on cache entry, shrinks eligible content by roughly 64%, and Cloudflare estimates it could free up petabytes of effective cache capacity using its Rust proxy framework Pingora; only successful, compressible responses of at least 4 KiB qualify.

The author argues agents now pick languages, frameworks and libraries on their own, sometimes ignoring explicit do-not-use instructions, potentially taking the role developers held in the decade-old book The New Kingmakers. item.title: [github_trending] agent-substrate/substrate
item.description: Agent Substrate is a secure-by-default execution runtime for autonomous agents that multiplexes many mostly-idle actors onto a small pool of workers. Its README claims 10x the sandbox density of standard container runtimes, sub-500ms resumes, over 500 suspend/resume activations per second, zero-trust kernel and network isolation, and support for microVMs and gVisor under one lifecycle API. It ships under Apache 2.0 and is not an officially supported Google product.
